messages.subject: Fix to set.seed over-run problem
parts:
Hi all,

Fix to a bug, already uploaded to PhyloWiki:


On Mon, Jun 6, 2016 at 7:50 PM, XXX wrote:
Hey Nick,

I can report that fixing the stratification files also fixed the problem.

I realized, though, that this was one of two errors I was getting leading to unsuccessful mapping. The other one is:

Error in set.seed(seed = seedval) : supplied seed is not a valid integer
In addition: Warning message:
In set.seed(seed = seedval) : NAs introduced by coercion to integer range

I’ve tried changing the seed value or removing it altogether, and I still get the message, but strangely only with certain trees (attached is a reproducible example with XXX and associated files).

Thanks (again!) for all your help with this,




Hi -- oh, this was an integer over-run, this never occurred on my small test examples.  To force the seed to be (a) changing every step but (b) deterministic based on the starting seed, I had a function calculating it by adding treepiece_seed_counter * treepiece_seed_counter_increment, and this was added incrementally through the list of tree pieces in a stratified analysis. This leads to the over-run on large problems I guess.

You can see the error here:
set.seed(2147483647)
set.seed(2147483648)

I'm adding a check that will use the remainder of (seed/2147483647) if the seed is over 2147483647...it looks like your file is working now, so I've uploaded it (and added the check several other places also).

Cheers, thanks for the bug report as always, you are giving the software a workout!

Cheers, Nick
